market_summary: Singapore bank earnings diverged sharply this week: OCBC beat estimates while DBS and UOB missed, with UOB showing the weakest price momentum despite a huge YoY profit jump. US tech is being whipsawed by idiosyncratic headlines — Nvidia is under a political/legal cloud (CEO scandal, FBI/Congressional scrutiny) layered on top of an already steep technical breakdown ahead of Nov 17 earnings, while Alphabet has been sold off hard on valuation worries even as consensus targets still imply large upside. Broader US indices (SPY/QQQ) rallied today, showing risk appetite is still intact for mega-caps outside the Nvidia/Alphabet idiosyncratic stories. Berkshire's aggressive buybacks signal management confidence even as underlying insurance earnings softened.

picks.thesis: Nvidia has a serious, fresh political/legal overhang (CEO personal scandal plus alleged China espionage ties) on top of an already-deteriorating technical picture (-22.5% in 1m, -25.3% off 52w high, below both the 50- and 200-day averages). Headline risk into the Nov 17 earnings date raises the chance of continued volatile downside before any fundamental re-rating, regardless of how bullish sell-side analysts remain long-term.
picks.news: Nov 8-9 2026: Nvidia board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted infidelity and was reportedly the target of a foreign intelligence effort; House Republicans are demanding answers over his ties to a China-linked businesswoman; Trump said the FBI is investigating; shares fell 4.2% on the news.
picks.risks: If the investigation clears Huang quickly or Washington scrutiny fades, the stock could snap back sharply given it is already 25% off highs and analysts see 80%+ upside to consensus targets — a short squeeze is a real risk, especially around the Nov 17 earnings print if results beat.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the only one of the three Singapore banks to beat Q3 estimates (profit +3% YoY vs consensus), and the stock reacted with a strong +3.4% day move, outperforming DBS and UOB which both missed. With a reasonable implied upside to consensus target (~8%) and 9 of 17 analysts at buy, the earnings beat should support a continued relative-strength trade versus its weaker peers over the next few weeks.
picks.news: Nov 8 2026: OCBC reported Q3 2026 net profit of S$2.04bn, up 3% YoY, beating analyst estimates — the only SG bank to do so this quarter.
picks.risks: All three SG banks are down 8-11% off 52-week highs on broader rate/margin concerns, and OCBC still screens -11.2% below its 52w high; if sector-wide net interest margin pressure or AI-loan-exposure worries (flagged Nov 9) intensify, even the earnings winner could get dragged down with peers.

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 profit expectations (S$1.25bn vs S$1.38bn forecast) despite a headline 182% YoY jump, and it is clearly the weakest of the three SG banks on price action: -7.7% in 1m, -12.1% in 3m, -18% off its 52-week high, trading below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages. Analyst sentiment is also the most lukewarm of the three (only 4 of 16 at buy, 10 at hold), suggesting continued relative underperformance versus DBS/OCBC.
picks.news: Nov 8 2026: UOB reported Q3 net profit of S$1.25bn, up 182% YoY but missing the S$1.38bn consensus forecast, extending a weak multi-month price trend.
picks.risks: The 182% YoY profit surge is a big number that could attract bargain-hunters given UOB is now the cheapest-looking SG bank and sits furthest below its consensus target (11.9% implied upside); any dovish rate read-through or sector-wide re-rating would hurt this short.

picks.thesis: Alphabet has been sold off aggressively (-17.3% 1m, -28.4% off 52w high) on valuation worries, including a sharp single-day 12.6% drop in late October, but the stock bounced +2% most recently and the consensus analyst target still implies ~39% upside with 53 of 58 analysts rating it buy. This looks like a potential oversold bounce/value opportunity, though the thesis is speculative given the news is primarily about concerns rather than a clear positive catalyst.
picks.news: Nov 9 2026 commentary: Alphabet stock down 8.8% YTD and 20%+ off its mid-October close amid persistent valuation concerns, despite an analyst base that remains overwhelmingly bullish on the name; one firm (Citizens) downgraded to Market Perform on Oct 29.
picks.risks: If the valuation concerns driving the sell-off are rooted in a genuine deceleration in ad or cloud growth (not covered in detail here), the stock could continue grinding lower rather than mean-revert; this is a lower-conviction, contrarian call given the news is thin on a positive catalyst.
